transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
It's a dizzy feeling, mostly when I stand up — I get light-headed and feel like I might faint. It happens when I get up from a chair or out of bed.
When did this first start for you, and do you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
Oh, it's been going on for months, I think. And no, I've never had any bad reactions to medicines as far as I know.
How much does this dizzy feeling affect your daily activities?

It's made me stop going to my Tuesday lunch club, because I worry about feeling faint on the bus. Each spell only lasts a minute or so, but it happens several times a day, and once I nearly fell and had to grab hold of the kitchen worktop.
Could you tell me about any medicines you take regularly or have taken recently, and any health problems you've had in the past?

Well, I have high blood pressure, and I've had that for about 15 years. I also have arthritis in both hips.

For tablets, I take a water tablet every morning, and I started a new blood-pressure one — amlodipine, 5 mg once a day — about two and a half weeks ago. The nurse added it because my readings were high. I also take a small tablet for my stomach each morning, though I can't remember the name of it, and paracetamol for the hip pain.
When you get that dizzy feeling, do you notice anything else happening at the same time?
No, I don't think so — there's no chest pain, no palpitations, and I haven't blacked out. My arms and legs feel fine too. It's just that swimmy, about-to-faint feeling, not like the room spinning.
When that swimmy, about-to-faint feeling comes on, where in your body do you notice it most?
It's mostly in my head — a light-headed, swimmy feeling, like I'm about to keel over. Not anywhere else in particular.
What worries you most about the dizzy feeling?
I'm worried the new blood-pressure tablet is causing it, and I'd like to know whether I should stop taking it.

Other than your high blood pressure and the arthritis in both hips, is there anything else in your past health — like other long-term conditions, past illnesses, operations, or hospital stays — that you’d like to add?
No, I don't think there's anything else. Just the blood pressure and the arthritis in my hips.
When did the dizzy feeling first start — did it come on suddenly or gradually, and was there anything happening at the time?

Actually, now that I think about it properly, it hasn't been months at all. It started about 10 days ago, roughly a week after I began that new blood-pressure tablet. It seemed to come on gradually rather than all at once.
Earlier you mentioned the dizzy feeling had been going on for months, and just now you said it started about 10 days ago — which of those is right?
It's the 10 days that's right — I got muddled earlier. It began about 10 days ago, roughly a week after I started the new blood-pressure tablet.

Thinking about all the medicines you take at the moment — is it just the new blood-pressure tablet, that tablet plus other regular medicines (including anything you buy yourself, like vitamins or painkillers), or are you not sure?

It's not just the new one — I take a few things. There's the new amlodipine, plus my water tablet every morning, and a small stomach tablet each morning that I can't remember the name of. And I take paracetamol, up to three times a day, for my hip pain.
Is there anything else you take, even now and then, that we haven’t talked about yet?
No, I don't think so. Just those — the amlodipine, the water tablet, the little stomach tablet, and the paracetamol.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
